title: Comparatives 5: Two Ways to Say "Than"
description: Russian has two equally correct ways to say 'than': чем + nominative (старше, чем брат) or the bare genitive with no preposition (старше брата). A pronoun or a whole clause forces чем; a short noun usually prefers the bare genitive.
descriptionRussian: В русском есть два равноправных способа сказать «чем»: «чем + именительный падеж» («старше, чем брат») или родительный падеж без предлога («старше брата»). Местоимение или целое предложение требуют «чем»; короткое существительное обычно предпочитает родительный.
intro: Two ways to say 'than', and they are usually interchangeable. One uses a word and a comma and leaves the other thing in its plain form; the other drops the word entirely and puts the thing in the genitive. Two situations force your hand: pronouns prefer the first, and comparing two whole ideas rather than two things requires it.
rules: Way 1: чем + nominative. The other thing stays in its plain dictionary form: Маша старше, чем её брат. In writing, put a comma before чем.
Way 2: the bare genitive. Drop чем and put the other thing straight into the genitive, with no comma: Маша старше своего брата.
With a pronoun, use чем + nominative: Я старше, чем он. The bare-genitive form старше его can sound unclear.
When 'than' joins two whole ideas (clauses), only чем works: Я ем больше, чем он спит.
examples: Маша старше, чем её брат. (Masha is older than her brother.) Way 1: чем + nominative брат.
Маша старше своего брата. (Masha is older than her brother.) Way 2: bare genitive брата. Same meaning.
Антон выше, чем его отец. (Anton is taller than his father.) Way 1 with чем + nominative отец.
Кофе дороже чая. (Coffee is more expensive than tea.) Way 2: bare genitive чая, a short simple noun.
Я старше, чем он. (I am older than he is.) Pronoun он, so чем is the clear choice.
Я ем больше, чем он спит. (I eat more than he sleeps.) Two whole ideas, so only чем works.

items.promptEnglish: Masha is older than her brother.
items.hint: Way 1: which little word means 'than' and lets the other thing stay in its plain form?
items.explanation: Way 1 is чем + nominative. The word чем means 'than' and lets брат stay in its plain dictionary form (её брат).

items.promptEnglish: Anton is older than his brother.
items.hint: Way 2: no чем here, so the other thing goes into the genitive.
items.explanation: There is no чем, so this is Way 2, the bare genitive. The noun goes straight into the genitive: брат → брата.

items.promptEnglish: Coffee is more expensive than tea.
items.hint: No чем in the sentence, so use the bare genitive. Чай ends in soft -й.
items.explanation: No чем, so the bare genitive is needed: чай → чая (soft -й becomes -я). Чая is a short, simple noun, which is exactly where the bare genitive feels most natural.

items.promptEnglish: I am older than he is.
items.hint: The other thing is a pronoun. Which way is the clear choice with a pronoun?
items.explanation: With a pronoun, чем + nominative is the clear choice, so the answer is чем and the pronoun stays as он. The bare-genitive form старше его can sound unclear, which is why чем is preferred here.

items.prompt: Я читаю больше, _____ он смотрит телевизор.
items.promptEnglish: I read more than he watches TV.
items.hint: 'Than' here joins two whole ideas. Which way works for clauses?
items.explanation: Here 'than' joins two whole ideas (I read / he watches TV), so only чем works. There is no single noun to put into the genitive, so the bare genitive is impossible.

items.promptEnglish: This table is longer than that one.
items.hint: No чем, so use the bare genitive. What is the genitive of тот?
items.explanation: No чем, so the bare genitive is needed. Тот (that one) goes into the genitive того.

items.promptEnglish: Coffee is more expensive than tea.
items.hint: The short way to say 'than' puts the noun in which case?
items.explanation: After a bare comparative, 'than' is expressed with the genitive: дороже чая. The alternative is чем + nominative (дороже, чем чай).

blanks: Лена выше своей _____ . (Lena is taller than her sister.)
Молоко дешевле _____ . (Milk is cheaper than juice.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Both sentences use Way 2, the bare genitive (no чем). The other thing goes straight into the genitive: сестра → сестры (feminine -а becomes -ы) and сок → сока (masculine, add -а).

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша поёт лучше, чем её брата.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha sings better than her brother.
errorCorrection.explanation: After чем (Way 1) the other thing stays in its plain dictionary form: чем её брат. The genitive брата belongs to the other way of saying 'than' (the bare genitive, used without чем: лучше её брата), so putting чем together with the genitive mixes the two ways.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton is taller than his brother.
errorCorrection.explanation: There is no чем here, so this is the bare genitive (Way 2): the other thing goes straight into the genitive, выше своего брата. The plain form свой брат is only used with чем (выше, чем свой брат). Свой changes to своего to match брата.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This book is more interesting than that one.
errorCorrection.explanation: There is no чем, so the bare genitive is needed: интереснее той. Та (that one, feminine) is the plain form, used only with чем (интереснее, чем та).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I work more than he sleeps.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Than' here joins two whole ideas (I work / he sleeps), so only чем works: больше, чем он спит. There is no single noun to put into the genitive, so the bare-genitive form его спит is impossible. Whenever 'than' links two clauses, you must use чем.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton is older than his brother.
minimalPairs.explanation: There is no чем, so the bare genitive is needed (Way 2): брат → брата. The plain form брат is used only with чем (старше, чем брат). Without чем, only the genitive брата works.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha is older than her sister.
minimalPairs.explanation: The sentence keeps её сестра in its plain form, so the 'than' word must be чем (Way 1). Just её would leave no word for 'than.' Чем + plain form is one complete way to say 'than.'

sentenceBuilding.translation: Masha is older than her brother. (Way 2: the bare genitive, no чем.)
sentenceBuilding.hint: No чем in the word bank, so use the bare genitive: brother goes into the genitive.

sentenceBuilding.translation: Anton is taller than his father. (Way 1: чем + plain form отец.)
sentenceBuilding.hint: The word чем is in the bank, so father stays in its plain form. A comma goes before чем.

sentenceBuilding.translation: I am older than he is. (Pronoun он, so чем is the clear choice.)
sentenceBuilding.hint: The other thing is a pronoun, so use чем and keep он in its plain form.

reviewVocab.definition: than (put it in front of the other thing, which stays in its plain dictionary form; a comma goes before чем in writing)
the bare genitive: the second way to say 'than'. Drop чем and put the other thing straight into the genitive, with no comma.
to compare; to say one thing is more or less than another (старше, выше, дороже + чем or the bare genitive)
reviewVocab.example: Когда мы сравниваем, можно сказать «старше, чем брат» или «старше брата».
